title: Quiz on User Stories and Acceptance Criteria

questions.text: According to the reference material, what is the standard format for a User Story?
questions.explanation: The reference material explicitly states the format: '“As a (type of user), I want to (perform some action) so that I (can achieve some goal/result/value).”'

answers.text: As a (type of user), I want to (perform some action) so that I (can achieve some goal/result/value).
Given (a context), When (an event occurs), Then (an outcome results).
The system shall (perform an action) when (a condition is met).
I need (a feature) to (solve a problem).

questions.text: What is the primary role of User Stories for agile teams, as described in the document?
questions.explanation: The document states: 'Para los equipos ágiles, User Stories son el primer método para identificar necesidades de los usuarios.'

questions.text: How do Acceptance Criteria contribute to the development process, according to the provided text?
questions.explanation: The text poses the question: '¿Cómo nos aseguramos de que las User Stories se han completado correctamente y conforme a las demandas de los clientes?' and immediately follows with 'Acceptance criteria', indicating their role in ensuring correct completion.

answers.text: They ensure User Stories are completed correctly and meet client demands.
They describe the user interface design.
They define the project's overall architecture.

questions.text: Based on the 'Scenario: usuario visualiza formulario “Brindar feedback”' described in the reference, which of the following is a required field in the feedback form?
questions.explanation: The acceptance criteria for the feedback form state: 'Entonces el sistema muestra el formulario “Brindar feedback” conteniendo los campos “Email”, “Nombre” y “Comentario” los cuales son requeridos.'

questions.text: According to the Behavior-Driven Development (BDD) section, what type of language should be avoided in scenario titles?
questions.explanation: The document explicitly advises: 'Evita palabras “verify”, “assert” o “should” en títulos de escenarios. Esas palabras ponen mas énfasis en la aseveración más que en el comportamiento, además se torna un título repetitivo.'
